rating.reasoning_summary: This strand represents a low-evolution meme cycle about SF party culture as a performative spectacle. The 'boundary object' is the SF tech/Twitter party itself—shoes off, non-technical friends excluded, sweatpants jiu-jitsu, hard drives as party props. The discourse is constructive (people are building shared mythology) but entirely aesthetic rather than dialectical. It functions as social signaling ('I was there' / 'I understand the joke') rather than knowledge production. The arc spans 2022-2025 but shows no conceptual evolution—just recurring variations on 'SF parties are weird/cringe/exclusive.' High cohesion (same community riffing) but zero utility beyond in-group entertainment.

essential_tweets.annotation: Origin: 2022 seed of 'kayfabe city'—SF as performance/unreality
The Viral Catalyst: March 2025 'sweatpants jiu-jitsu party' that sparked the meme wave
Name-dropping: Establishing this as a 'twitterati' scene event
FOMO Signal: The social anxiety of missing the mythologized party
Counter-signal: Attending makes you 'ngmi'—ironic status inversion
The Artifact: 'Non-technical friend' meme—peak gatekeeping satire (2531 likes)
Hard Drive Girl: Visual embodiment of 'tech party aesthetic' absurdity
Shoes-off norm: Physical marker of SF party culture
Tourist's Dilemma: 'You'll hate it but need to see it'—framing parties as spectacle
Feet Guy joke: The meme's final form—pure absurdist riffing
